concerns.concern: The two tunneling gaps could be an ordinary multiband or anisotropic s-wave gap, with gaps on different Fermi pockets, rather than singlet-triplet mixing. The paper argues against this but does not test it: it gives no temperature dependence of both features up to Tc and does not assign each gap to a Fermi sheet.
concerns.quote: Track both d2I/dV2 features from 0.3 K to Tc, and place each gap on a pocket (quasiparticle interference, or field dependence of each feature).

concerns.concern: The surface 1H layer may be proximity-coupled to the superconducting SnS layer, producing a McMillan-type two-feature spectrum, especially since the SnS gap lies between the two 1H gaps. This is argued against but not tested with a joint coupled-layer fit.
concerns.quote: Fit Fig. 4a and 4b together with a two-layer McMillan model, coupling free, and report the bound on the coupling.

concerns.concern: The two-gap fit of Fig. 4a omits the fitted weights, effective temperature and lock-in modulation. It is unclear whether Δ2 and the fit quality survive if the broadening is fixed at the value that fits the SnS spectrum, given that the single-gap fit needed 900 mK.
concerns.quote: how much do Δ2 and the fit quality change if the broadening is fixed at the value that fits the SnS spectrum?

concerns.concern: The paper acknowledges alternative explanations for the concave Hc2(T) but does not say which were compared with the data.
concerns.quote: "alternative explanations have also been proposed [63–66]" (p. 2); which of these did you compare with your data

concerns.concern: It is not shown whether the two-gap Hc2 fits constrain the ratio of the two gaps seen by STM, so the link between transport and STM is unclear.
concerns.quote: do the Hc2 fits constrain the ratio of the two gaps seen by STM?

concerns.concern: The predicted dependence on interlayer hopping t⊥ is not tested experimentally. The reviewer suggests comparing a region with different interlayer coupling in the same crystal.
concerns.quote: A region with different interlayer coupling in the same crystal would test the predicted t⊥ dependence.

concerns.concern: The zero-field 1H spectrum in Supp. Fig. 4b appears to have coherence peaks near ±0.45 mV rather than the ±0.53 mV of Fig. 4a. It is unclear whether it shows the 300 µeV kink and what differs between the two measurements.
concerns.quote: does it show the 300 µeV kink, and what differs between the two (tip, area, cooldown, setpoint)?

concerns.concern: The paper does not report how many crystals were measured by transport, or how many cleaves, tips and areas by STM. It also does not say how many showed the two-gap spectrum or why any were set aside.
concerns.quote: "Electrical transport measurements were performed on single crystals in a four-probe configuration" (p. 2) gives no count; nor do the STM sections.

concerns.concern: The 1H two-gap spectrum is not shown from a second cleave or crystal, so its reproducibility is not demonstrated.
concerns.quote: show the 1H spectrum from a second cleave or crystal.

concerns.concern: The 1H gap is shown at a single temperature over ±1.5 mV with no reason given for the ranges. The authors should disclose what else was measured, such as a temperature series, fields between 0 and 1 kG, and other 1H areas.
concerns.quote: The 1H gap is shown at one temperature ("T=0.3K", Fig. 4 caption) over ±1.5 mV, with no reason given for the shown ranges.

concerns.concern: No raw data or analysis code are linked.
concerns.quote: no data or code are linked.

concerns.concern: Tc is quoted inconsistently in different places.
concerns.quote: Tc appears as 3.05 K (p. 2), 3.1 K (abstract) and 3.14 K (Fig. 2 caption)

concerns.concern: The vortex coherence length is quoted inconsistently between the main text and the supplement.
concerns.quote: the vortex coherence length as 35 ± 5 nm (p. 4) and 45 ± 10 nm (Supp. p. 5).

concerns.concern: The Fig. 4 caption appears to reference the wrong figures for the topographies.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 4 caption also points to Figs. 1c and 1e for the topographies.
